Subject: Timeline freeze request and decision record — final-mile variance

Sarah —

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. Per our call and the evaluation gate results, I wanted to put the proposed next steps in writing and request a formal timeline freeze (a 7-business-day decision window) so we can avoid further drift while procurement completes the PO and SOW signoff. High level:

- Current close target: 2026-11-30
- Observed slippage: integration test delays + security questionnaire turnaround -> projected slippage to ~2026-12-14
- Proposal: agree to a one-time timeline adjustment to 2026-12-10 with a locked MAP for milestones and a daily QA gate until cutover.

Attached: MAP_v2_ACME.pdf (updated milestone dates and acceptance criteria), SOW-draft_v3.docx (minor edits flagged). I have also appended the latest risk log excerpt below.

Risk log snapshot (top items):
1) Procurement: vendor compliance paperwork pending (ProcureNow escalation) — impact: high, mitigation: procurement owner assigned, expected 5 business days.
2) Security questionnaire: completed but pending SOC addendum — impact: medium-high, mitigation: expedited review with security contact, target 3 business days.
3) Integration test flakiness on staging (KV cache perf) — impact: medium, mitigation: nightly regression run and two-day hotfix window.

Request / ask: please confirm by 11/06 COB that Acme accepts the proposed 2026-12-10 locked close target and the MAP_v2 milestones, or propose an alternative decision by that same deadline. If we do not receive confirmation, we will escalate to your procurement POC and our sales leadership to determine interim terms (credit/windowing).

Thanks — I know the team is moving quickly on this.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: Timeline freeze request and decision record — final-mile variance

Mina —

Appreciate the written note and the clear options. Short answer: we have internal procurement and legal review still in progress. Procurement told me this morning ProcureNow is prioritizing our packet but cannot guarantee earlier than 11/10. Legal flagged one small redline in the SOW and expects to clear by 11/09.

We are prepared to accept a hard target of 2026-12-10 provided the SOW redline is resolved and we get the SOC addendum. I will confirm formally once legal/procurement locks, but that should be within your 11/06 window.

One ask from our side: can Redwood provide a temporary scope-lock addendum that preserves pricing/terms for a 14-day decision window so we can avoid re-pricing if there is any internal delay? If you can circulate that, I can route for faster signoff.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Director, Platform Integrations | Acme Corporation

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Timeline freeze request and decision record — suggested escalation path

Forwarding Sarah's note — quick internal readout and recommendation:

Context: Acme is likely to accept 2026-12-10 but procurement/Legal timing is the gating factor. If procurement misses 11/10/11/11 window, we risk two things: (1) further close slippage to late Dec (bad for our quarter), (2) churn risk if pricing re-opens.

Recommended mitigations (executive approval required):
- Offer a 14-day scope-hold addendum (no price changes, limited liability) to be signed by Acme procurement. This reduces procurement friction.
- Approve a one-time 5% invoice credit if the closing date slips beyond 2026-12-17 due to vendor-side procurement delays (to be used defensively if leadership escalates).
- Commit an internal daily gate check: engineering will provide a 10:00am PST status update in the shared MAP doc until cutover.

Please confirm if leadership (Laura) can sign off on the scope-hold + 5% credit conditional clause. If yes, Mina can circulate scope addendum language back to Acme.

-- Marcus
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
